text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week slide that's cost the stock 14%. The decline tracks a broader pullback in refining stocks amid falling crude oil prices—U.S. oil dropped to $82 per barrel, well below the $91 Brent price, compressing the profit margin refiners earn by processing crude into products like gasoline and diesel. Refineries are running at 97.5% capacity with ample fuel in storage, meaning high throughput isn't translating to stronger margins in this price environment.

Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and Iranian mines in the Strait of Hormuz—haven't lifted oil prices despite disruption risks, suggesting markets aren't pricing in sustained supply cuts. The absence of a bull case in the data, combined with weak crude spreads, has kept refining plays under pressure.
